from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    freq = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row)
    colors = [c for c, _ in freq.most_common()]
    base = colors[0]
    line = colors[1] if len(colors) > 1 else base

    # Grid separators are rows/columns largely made of the second-most-common
    # color. The outer edge can also be a separator.
    rs = [r for r in range(h)
          if sum(x == line for x in grid[r]) >= 0.55 * w]
    cs = [c for c in range(w)
          if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= 0.45 * h]

    # Fall back to regularly spaced boundaries when an outer boundary uses
    # the background color rather than the separator color.
    def extend(bounds, limit):
        if len(bounds) >= 2:
            gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(bounds, bounds[1:])]
            step = Counter(gaps).most_common(1)[0][0]
            out = set(bounds)
            for b in list(bounds):
                while b - step >= 0 and b - step not in out:
                    b -= step
                    out.add(b)
                b = max(bounds)
                while b + step < limit and b + step not in out:
                    b += step
                    out.add(b)
            return sorted(out)
        return bounds

    rs = extend(rs, h)
    cs = extend(cs, w)

    if len(rs) < 2 or len(cs) < 2:
        return [[base]]

    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(rs, rs[1:]):
        row = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(cs, cs[1:]):
            corners = [grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1]]
            value = corners[0] if len(set(corners)) == 1 and corners[0] != base else base
            row.append(value)
        out.append(row)

    # Discard trailing rows/columns that contain no extracted feature.
    while len(out) > 1 and all(v == base for v in out[-1]):
        out.pop()
    while len(out[0]) > 1 and all(row[-1] == base for row in out):
        for row in out:
            row.pop()

    # If there are no four-corner matches, a separator may itself encode a
    # one-row result through matching colors at adjacent intersections.
    if all(v == base for row in out for v in row):
        for r in range(h):
            vals = []
            for c0, c1 in zip(cs, cs[1:]):
                a, b = grid[r][c0], grid[r][c1]
                vals.append(a if a == b and a != line else base)
            if any(v != base for v in vals):
                return [vals]
    return out
